subject: Atlas Finance DPA - model improvement prohibition & onshore KMS audit request
messages:
From: Lena Holst <lena.holst@atlasfinance.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 14:15:00 +0100
Subject: Draft DPA + ask on model improvement prohibition and KMS residency
Attachments: Atlas-DPA-Draft-0909.pdf

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's hosted offering last week. We're starting legal review and have a couple of non-standard asks related to AI/LLM usage that we'd like to lock down in the DPA before procurement will approve pilots. High level: 1) a clear prohibition on using our content to improve or retrain models (we call this a model improvement prohibition), 2) onshore key management or a documented path to onshore KMS residency for EU customer keys, and 3) an attestation or evidence pack showing no adaptive learning pipelines touching customer prompts/responses.

I've attached a draft DPA (not redlined yet) — can your team confirm whether Redwood will accept a model-improvement prohibition clause that applies to hosted API traffic, and if so, what operational evidence you can provide? Specifically: 
- A short description of the technical controls that prevent customer interactions from being used in model updates.
- Whether KV/prefix caches or telemetry ever flow to training pipelines.
- For KMS: is customer key material eligible to be stored in an EU onshore KMS, or do you have an onshore HSM option? If not, what's the documented migration path?

Procurement would like replies and any evidence by end of week to keep the timeline. Copied procurement@atlasfinance.com for traceability.

Thanks,
Lena Holst
Head of Vendor Risk, Atlas Finance

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Holst <lena.holst@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 16:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + ask on model improvement prohibition and KMS residency

Hi Lena — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear list. We can, in practice, support a strong model improvement prohibition for hosted customers. Below are high-level answers; Marissa and David are copied to provide legal and ops-level specifics and any requested documentation.

Quick summary:
- Model improvement prohibition: Yes, we offer an explicit contractual prohibition that prevents Redwood from using customer-provided prompts/responses for training or model parameter updates for hosting customers who opt in. We also offer an operational evidence pack.
- Technical controls: our serving runtime supports an opt-out flag on a per-customer basis that prevents interaction telemetry from feeding into offline model training jobs. We also use strict routing policies to segregate tenant logs.
- Caching/telemetry: ephemeral KV caches used for inference are never persisted into training data stores by default. Telemetry for usage/debugging is sampled and can be disabled for customers with the prohibition.
- KMS residency: we currently support customer-managed keys via integration with EU cloud KMS providers and offer a roadmap for on-prem KMS/HSM for enterprise customers. We'll confirm timelines for formal onshore key residency guarantees.

Next steps: David will attach the ops evidence pack and a KMS residency diagram. Marissa will follow up with proposed DPA language and any exceptions. If you can share procurement redlines, we can route them through Legal quickly.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Holst <lena.holst@atlasfinance.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 +0100
Subject: Ops evidence pack + KMS residency diagram
Attachments: kms-residency-diagram.png

Hi Lena — following up with the operational detail you asked for. Attached is a one-page KMS/residency diagram and below is a brief attestation we use with customers when they opt into the model improvement prohibition.

Attestation (summary):
- Indexed prompts and responses are retained only in ephemeral serving caches and in access-controlled logs required for billing and debugging. These logs are logically separated per customer.
- No automated pipeline moves customer interaction logs into training corpora. A manual gating process, with approvals and audit trails, exists for any data extraction — and it is disabled for customers who contractually opt out of model improvement.
- Telemetry sampling is configurable; when opt-out is enabled sampling is set to 0% for training-oriented telemetry.

Operational notes:
- For EU customers we can integrate with customer's KMS (bring-your-own-key) on Azure Key Vault or Google Cloud KMS with keys resident in EU regions.
- For customers requiring on-prem or HSM-backed residency we have an enterprise integration path; current delivery estimates depend on contract size and security review (typical 8–12 weeks after commercial agreement).

If Atlas would like, we can produce a short PDF evidence pack including audit log schema examples and the manual gating approval records template.

Regards,
David Kim
Director, Platform Security & Compliance

From: Procurement Team <procurement@atlasfinance.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:23:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Draft DPA + ask on model improvement prohibition and KMS residency
Attachments: procurement-redlines-0915.pdf

Hi Sofia, David, Marissa — thanks for the quick responses and the diagram. Procurement has reviewed and provided a first pass of redlines (attached). Main concerns from legal/risk are: 
1) The draft needs a clear evergreen clause that prevents use of Atlas data for model updates now and in the future, including downstream model derivatives.
2) Evidence: SOC 2 plus a short evidence pack as described by David (audit log examples, gating workflows).
3) KMS: we are pushing for contractual commitment that customer-managed keys will remain resident within the EU, with a mechanism to escalate if keys are moved. If Redwood cannot guarantee an onshore HSM, we need the documented migration timeline and milestone-based acceptance criteria in the SOW.

We also flagged a market-standard audit right for a third-party assessor (once per year, limited scope) to validate the enforcement of the model-improvement prohibition. Can your legal team comment on whether Redwood will accept an annual scoped assessment limited to the prohibition controls?

Our timeline is: we need a redlined DPA + evidence pack and confirmation on audit access by end of next week to keep the pilot start date.

Best,
Procurement Team
Atlas Finance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Holst <lena.holst@atlasfinance.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + ask on model improvement prohibition and KMS residency

Hi Lena / Atlas procurement — thanks for the clear feedback and the attached redlines. We reviewed internally and propose the following path to keep things moving: 

1) Contract language: Redwood will accept a model improvement prohibition clause with the following scope: a) Redwood will not use Atlas customer data (prompts/responses/attachments) to modify model weights, fine-tune, or otherwise adapt models for the purpose of improving model performance, and b) Redwood will not incorporate Atlas customer data into any derivative training datasets. We will propose specific DPA wording in a tracked redline PDF by EOD.

2) Evidence pack: David will prepare the evidence pack (SOC 2 section references, audit log schema, gating workflow template). We'll provide the pack as a constrained set of artifacts (PDF + diagrams).

3) Annual scoped assessment: Redwood is open to a limited annual third-party assessment focused exclusively on enforcement of the model improvement prohibition (controls, gating approvals, and key residency). We will require a mutually agreed scope and an approved assessor list; Redwood's legal team will propose a nondisruptive process (read-only access to specific logs and control evidence).

4) KMS residency/SOW milestones: For EU-resident keys we confirm support for BYOK with EU-region cloud KMS providers. If Atlas requires HSM-backed on-prem keys, we'll include a milestone-driven migration schedule in the SOW with acceptance criteria (delivery window estimated 8–12 weeks post-signature). We'll include escalation clauses for unauthorized key movement.

Next steps: I'll upload a tracked-redline DPA and Marissa/Legal's recommended language to the DocuSign/drive link shared in related_links. Can Atlas confirm preferred assessor firms for the annual scope so we can evaluate conflict of interest? Once we have your confirmation, we will prepare a final bundle for signature.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
